column3: The Hebrew presents taking refuge as a completed action; BSB uses the present.
The Hebrew has a singular he, where BSB uses they.
The Hebrew uses a verb of rescuing in the second clause; BSB says plundered.
The Hebrew names his soul and life and pictures his honor dwelling in dust; BSB first says me.
The Hebrew says awake to me and You have commanded judgment; BSB addresses my God and commands ordaining judgment.
The Hebrew commands returning on high; BSB says take Your seat.
The Hebrew names kidneys rather than minds.
The Hebrew leaves the subjects as pronouns without explicitly naming God.
The Hebrew explicitly says for him before preparing deadly weapons.
The Hebrew leaves the subject unnamed; BSB supplies the wicked man.
The Hebrew names his head and crown separately; BSB first says himself.
